name: The Great Guide to Crafting and Gathering
description: Recipe books, gathering sources and guides. Import with the module's prompt, or from this compendium.

mastercrafted.description: Refiners fill these ledgers fast, and old shops keep them in tall stacks.
Forge sparks have pocked its brown cover and steel plate.
Loose paper patterns, soft from tracing, bulge between its pages.
Each owner carves a small mark into the pale wooden covers before passing it on.
Stray threads of every color mark the pages a tailor turns to most.
Its margins are crowded with drawings of gem cuts, none larger than a fingernail.
A thick blue book, its pages warped and spotted where stillroom steam has reached them.
Nothing on the green cover or spine says what the notebook holds.
Thumbs have worn the rune on its purple cover smooth.
Every page starts with one neat line, copied in rows below by less steady hands.
Bound on a coil of wire, the blue notebook lies flat on any bench.
The plain orange book falls open by itself at the bread recipes.

text.content: This shield was the last thing standing at a gate whose name is forgotten. Its face is dented in a hundred places, and each dent is polished bright by the hands of soldiers who touch it before a battle.
The plates of this armor are gray and cold, and frost forms on them in a warm room. Whoever wears it casts a shadow a little too long, as if the sun stood lower for them alone.

The edge of this axe has never been sharpened. Smiths who look closely say that it has no edge at all, only a line where the steel stops, and that the line is thinner than anything they know how to grind.
The inside of this satchel is darker than its leather can account for. It shifts on the shoulder like a sleeping animal, and it is always a little warm.
The hide stays wet in the driest desert and smells of deep water. Its suckers open and close slowly along the sleeves, and they leave ring marks on any table the armor is laid upon.
The soles of these boots have never worn thin. Dust from every road they have walked lies in the seams, in colors that no single country has, and it cannot be brushed out.
A staff cut from a tree older than any forest now standing. It puts out a single green leaf each spring, in whatever country it happens to be, and drops it again in the fall.
The back of this shield is rough bark, and the front is smooth heartwood with rings too many to count. Set down on bare earth, it leans toward the nearest water.
The string of this bow hums before a storm, hours before the first cloud. Archers who have drawn it say the air smells scorched afterward, and that birds stay out of the sky above it for a day.
White cloth sewn with feathers that are warm to the touch. In a dark room the raiment gives off the gray light of the hour before sunrise, and roosters crow when it is carried past.
The cloth of this banner has been cut by a thousand blades and shows no mend. It stirs when there is no wind, and soldiers say it leans toward whichever side of a field is losing heart.
A gray cloak with nothing remarkable about it, which is the remarkable thing. People asked to describe its wearer afterward can never agree on a height, a face or a voice.
A clear stone cut in the shape of a heart, hung on a gold chain. It throws colors on the wall in a dark room, and the colors move like something breathing.
A plain gold band that is warm at dawn and cool by dusk, every day, wherever it is kept. The engraving inside it is a single line that runs around the ring and meets itself.
A narrow gold circlet set with one pale stone. The stone is never the same color twice, and those who wear the crown stop blinking as often as other people do.
A single mouthful of pale gold liquid in a stoppered bottle. It moves more slowly than water should, and bubbles that rise in it take most of a minute to reach the top.
A round flask of thick red glass that is always a little heavier than it looks. However long it is held upside down, one last drop stays in the neck and will not fall.
A leather belt of small glass vials, each a different color and none of them labeled. The vials clink against each other in a pattern that is almost a tune, and they are never quite full.
A smooth brown stone the size of a plum, taken from the stomach of an animal nobody has been able to name. It is lighter than it looks, and it floats in wine but sinks in water.
Three clear drops sealed in a bead of glass, which do not run together however the bead is turned. Flies that land on the bead do not get up again.
A vial of dark glass with a silver snake coiled around its neck. The snake's head rests on the stopper, and its eyes are open at dawn and shut for the rest of the day.
A short rod of blue metal with seven rings around it, each cold to a different degree. In still weather the rings turn slowly on their own, and never all in the same direction.
A disc of red metal stamped with a mark that hurts a little to look at directly. Four older marks are worn smooth beneath it, and nobody living can say what those four sealed.
A thin wand of black wood capped with a violet stone. Doors swing shut when it is carried through a house, and candles near it burn straight up without a flicker.
A blue book of maps that is never the same thickness twice. New pages appear at the back whenever its owner crosses a border, already inked and already dry.
A short scroll bound with a gold cord that has no knot. The writing inside is a single sentence, and people who have seen one say that the sentence was shorter than they expected.
No two pages of this book are in the same hand. The ink is still wet on the last page however long the book has been closed, and the last page is never the same one.
A harness of straps and brass around a mainspring the size of a fist. It ticks in time with its wearer's pulse, and it goes on ticking for an hour after it is taken off.
A small key with no teeth, only a smooth blade. Held near a lock it grows the teeth that lock needs, and it loses them again when it is taken away.
A crossbow stock fitted with a coil of copper where the bow should be. The coil crackles in dry weather, and compasses carried near it point at it and nowhere else.
A black iron cauldron with a dent in its rim, older than the kingdom it was found in. It is warm before any fire is lit under it, and it has never once boiled over.
Five courses on one great platter, each cut from a beast that cooks do not expect to see twice in a lifetime. The smell of it carries a mile, and it stays hot until the last plate is empty.
A small green box of many drawers, each holding a spice that grows in only one valley. However much is used, the drawers are full again by the time the pot is washed.

mastercrafted.description: Each page follows one great work from bare stock to the finished piece.
